argument: The body must read as one produced ink object before it reads as an interaction surface. The shell, perforations, and fold paths must be geometry, not CSS decoration.
A first touch is a latent call, not a mark. The second sufficiently separated witness must be the only route to a committed fold, with pointer, touch, keyboard, and control paths equivalent.

With readout, controls, caption, annotations, and prose hidden, the body must leave the prior raster plate, relief membrane, and fragment archive. It must not collapse into a node diagram or click counter.
The first call must preserve the exact body signature. A valid reply must alter fold paths, shell pressure, and perforation openings in actual replay geometry.
Four exchanges must compound in one body. Delete must reconstruct the exact preceding body and release must restore the deterministic seed.
The custom Canvas polygon, void, and fold vocabulary must be generated by the engine and replay state, not by an imported brush library, texture, screenshot, or static overlay.

little-critters is translated from situated proximity and reciprocal attention into a two-site material call-and-response. Animals, eyes, characters, paper, palette, composition, code, and API surface are refused.

Delete v043 if a first touch mutates the body, if a self-reply commits, if the fold is cosmetic, if the blind body reads as a generic diagram or seal, if later exchanges reset, or if exact lifting fails.
